subject: Re: Commercial terms for Clearbridge migration — incentives and packaging
messages:
From: Ben Willis <ben.willis@clearbridge.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearbridge.io>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Migration economics — initial ask

Marcus,

Thanks for the run through earlier. We ran the numbers with the finance and infra teams and have two quick asks to get internal approval to proceed to a pilot: 1) a 3‑month onboarding credit to cover engineering effort and egress while we validate runtime; 2) a blended unit price match to our incumbent for the first 6 months (we can share the usage profile).

Key constraints: procurement wants an explicit carveout for post‑pilot SLA credits, and our CTO wants a plan that doesn’t lock us into a heavy prepay. We prefer a combination of an operational credit + committed seats rather than a big up‑front prepay.

I attached a simple TCO workbook (see Clearbridge_Migration_TCO.xlsx) — happy to walk through numbers next week.

Best,
Ben Willis
VP, Cloud Ops
Clearbridge

--
Attachment: Clearbridge_Migration_TCO.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Willis <ben.willis@clearbridge.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration economics — initial ask

Ben — thanks for the clarity and the workbook. Looping in Neha (pricing) and Karthik (solutions) so we can put a succinct counterproposal together. A few quick notes from my side before we model: 

- We can structure a 3‑month onboarding credit that’s applied as a usage rebate (reduces invoice, preserves reporting).
- For the 6‑month price match, we generally do a matched effective rate via a combination of a transient discount + an onboarding credit rather than direct one‑for‑one matching on list price. That lets us avoid long prepay commitments.
- We can include a one‑time migration credit to cover integration engineering (SOW line item) — that can be tied to milestones in SOW_v2.docx.

Neha/Karthik — can you prepare two compact scenarios: (A) minimal commitment — onboarding rebate + 6‑month blended match that scales by token volume, and (B) committed seats (12‑month) with a stepped rebate and lower unit price. If Ben’s team prefers no prepay, (A) should be our anchor.

I’ll schedule a 30‑min call next week to review.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: SOW_v2.docx (document, 95KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Willis <ben.willis@clearbridge.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration economics — initial ask

Hi all — I ran two scenarios off Marcus’s ask (attached below as summarized bullets). Ben — calling out assumptions so we’re aligned: we used your workbook volumes and a 95th percentile per‑token distribution you shared.

Scenario A — Low commitment (preferred if no prepay):
- 3‑month onboarding credit = $75k applied as invoice rebate (covers egress + integration)
- 6‑month blended price match via a 20% transient discount on hosted usage with automatic volume tiering (kicks in at 500M tokens/month)
- No SLA buy; standard hosted SLA applies
- Migration credit paid upon production cutover

Scenario B — Committed seats (12‑month):
- 12‑month commitment at 40% off list for committed capacity + 2 months free during onboarding (applied as credit)
- Additional migration credit of $40k to offset professional services
- SLA uplift available for an add‑on fee (we can show numbers)

Risks/Notes:
- If Clearbridge requires contractual fallback on price parity after 6 months, we need a narrowly scoped clause (e.g., ability to exit on 30 days with pro‑rated refund of unused committed capacity).
- For procurement: we’ll accept a limited carveout for post‑pilot SLA credits (up to $X) but avoid open‑ended liabilities.

I can convert these into clean bullets for the call and attach a short term sheet.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Willis <ben.willis@clearbridge.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearbridge.io>, ops@clearbridge.io
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration economics — initial ask

Neha / Marcus — thanks for the fast turnaround and two scenarios — helpful. Procurement prefers Scenario A but would like the onboarding credit increased to $90k (they want to cover a small consultant run as well). Two quick asks from our side before the call:

1) Can you make the transient discount explicitly capped at a 6‑month window and documented as a blended effective rate in the term sheet? We want a clear comparison line in the SOW.
2) For the migration credit, is it possible to route payment as a rebate (invoice credit) rather than a separate delivery milestone? That speeds approvals.

If you can update the term sheet with those points and a short one‑page appendix that maps to the workbook, procurement will sign off to move to pilot approvals.

Best,
Ben

--
On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 07:45 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben — noted. We’ll update the term sheet to show: (i) 6‑month capped transient discount and blended effective rate table; (ii) onboarding + migration credits applied as invoice rebates. Neha / Karthik taking action.
>
> Marcus

--
Attachment: Clearbridge_Migration_TCO.xlsx (updated, 121KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Willis <ben.willis@clearbridge.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration economics — initial ask

Ben — quick note ahead of the call: we’ve drafted a one‑page appendix that maps the blended effective rate to your workbook and caps the transient discount at 6 months as requested. We’ll apply the onboarding + migration credits as invoice rebates (they show on month 1 and month 3 respectively). I’ll share the term sheet and appendix link in the next email and include a short implementation runbook (pivoting on whether you run Hosted API vs Dedicated pool during pilot).

Looking forward to the call.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
